topicTitle: Statements and Arguments — Strong vs Weak

questions.question:
Statement: Should plastic bags be banned?

Arguments:
I. Yes, they pollute the environment and harm animals.
II. No, they are very cheap.

Which of the following is correct?
options: Only argument II is strong
Only argument I is strong
Both arguments I and II are strong
Neither argument I nor II is strong
questions.explanation: Environmental harm is relevant and serious (I strong); low price is a minor point against that harm (II weak). Answer: Only argument I is strong.

questions.question:
Statement: Should voting be made compulsory?

Arguments:
I. No, because many people dislike politics.
II. Yes, it will raise voter turnout and make governments more representative.

Which of the following is correct?
options: Only argument II is strong
Only argument I is strong
Both arguments I and II are strong
Neither argument I nor II is strong
questions.explanation: Higher turnout and wider representation are direct, important effects (II strong); disliking politics is a personal attitude, not a consequence (I weak). Answer: Only argument II is strong.

questions.question:
Statement: Should school students be given daily homework?

Arguments:
I. Yes, regular practice improves learning.
II. Yes, because teachers like to check notebooks.

Which of the following is correct?
options: Only argument II is strong
Both arguments I and II are strong
Neither argument I nor II is strong
Only argument I is strong
questions.explanation: Better learning is the central purpose of homework (I strong); teachers' liking is irrelevant (II weak). Answer: Only argument I is strong.

questions.question:
Statement: Should smoking be banned in public places?

Arguments:
I. No, smokers will feel unhappy.
II. Yes, passive smoke harms the health of non-smokers.

Which of the following is correct?
options: Only argument I is strong
Both arguments I and II are strong
Only argument II is strong
Neither argument I nor II is strong
questions.explanation: Harm to non-smokers' health is relevant and serious (II strong); smokers' unhappiness is minor (I weak). Answer: Only argument II is strong.

questions.question:
Statement: Should the government provide free vaccination to all children?

Arguments:
I. Yes, it prevents serious diseases and protects the whole community.
II. Yes, because other countries do it.

Which of the following is correct?
options: Only argument II is strong
Both arguments I and II are strong
Only argument I is strong
Neither argument I nor II is strong
questions.explanation: Disease prevention is a strong, specific reason (I). Copying other countries gives no reason of its own (II weak). Answer: Only argument I is strong.

questions.question:
Statement: Should mobile phones be allowed inside examination halls?

Arguments:
I. No, because phones are costly.
II. No, because they can be used for cheating.

Which of the following is correct?
options: Only argument I is strong
Only argument II is strong
Both arguments I and II are strong
Neither argument I nor II is strong
questions.explanation: Cheating directly damages the fairness of an exam (II strong); the cost of phones is irrelevant (I weak). Answer: Only argument II is strong.

questions.question:
Statement: Should cash be completely replaced by digital payments?

Arguments:
I. Yes, digital payments are faster and leave a traceable record.
II. No, many villages do not have reliable internet or smartphones.

Which of the following is correct?
options: Both arguments I and II are strong
Only argument I is strong
Only argument II is strong
Neither argument I nor II is strong
questions.explanation: Speed and traceability are real advantages (I strong); lack of access in villages is a serious practical objection (II strong). Answer: Both arguments I and II are strong.

questions.question:
Statement: Should the retirement age be raised to 65?

Arguments:
I. Yes, people now live longer and remain productive for longer.
II. No, it will reduce job openings for young people.

Which of the following is correct?
options: Only argument I is strong
Only argument II is strong
Neither argument I nor II is strong
Both arguments I and II are strong
questions.explanation: Longer, productive lives are relevant (I strong) and reduced openings for the young are a real effect (II strong). Answer: Both arguments I and II are strong.

questions.question:
Statement: Should the examination system be abolished?

Arguments:
I. Yes, exams cause stress to some students.
II. No, exams are the only way to ever know anything about a student.

Which of the following is correct?
options: Only argument I is strong
Only argument II is strong
Both arguments I and II are strong
Neither argument I nor II is strong
questions.explanation: Stress for some students is too small a reason to abolish exams (I weak); "the only way to ever know anything" is an exaggeration (II weak). Answer: Neither argument I nor II is strong.

questions.question:
Statement: Should advertisements of fast food aimed at children be banned?

Arguments:
I. Yes, children are easily influenced and such food harms their health.
II. No, advertisements are a source of revenue for television channels.

Which of the following is correct?
options: Only argument II is strong
Both arguments I and II are strong
Only argument I is strong
Neither argument I nor II is strong
questions.explanation: Child health is important and the link to advertising is direct (I strong); channel revenue is a narrow commercial interest set against that (II weak). Answer: Only argument I is strong.

questions.question:
Statement: Should private vehicles be banned in the city centre?

Arguments:
I. No, some people enjoy driving.
II. Yes, it will reduce pollution and traffic jams.

Which of the following is correct?
options: Only argument I is strong
Only argument II is strong
Both arguments I and II are strong
Neither argument I nor II is strong
questions.explanation: Less pollution and congestion are major public benefits (II strong); enjoying driving is a personal preference (I weak). Answer: Only argument II is strong.

questions.question:
Statement: Should students be given pocket money?

Arguments:
I. Yes, because everyone should have some money.
II. No, because it is bad.

Which of the following is correct?
options: Neither argument I nor II is strong
Only argument I is strong
Only argument II is strong
Both arguments I and II are strong
questions.explanation: "Everyone should" is vague (I weak) and "it is bad" gives no reason (II weak). Answer: Neither argument I nor II is strong.

questions.question:
Statement: Should the government increase the tax on tobacco products?

Arguments:
I. Yes, because tobacco companies are rich.
II. Yes, higher prices reduce consumption and raise revenue for health care.

Which of the following is correct?
options: Only argument II is strong
Only argument I is strong
Both arguments I and II are strong
Neither argument I nor II is strong
questions.explanation: Reducing consumption and funding health care are direct, important effects (II strong); the wealth of companies is not a reason for the tax (I weak). Answer: Only argument II is strong.

questions.question:
Statement: Should junk food be sold in school canteens?

Arguments:
I. No, it harms children's health and concentration.
II. Yes, children like it.

Which of the following is correct?
options: Only argument II is strong
Both arguments I and II are strong
Neither argument I nor II is strong
Only argument I is strong
questions.explanation: Harm to health and concentration is specific and important (I strong); liking is a preference (II weak). Answer: Only argument I is strong.

questions.question:
Statement: Should the government stop all imports of foreign goods?

Arguments:
I. Yes, it will protect domestic industries.
II. No, India does not produce many essential inputs and others may retaliate with trade barriers on its exports.

Which of the following is correct?
options: Only argument I is strong
Both arguments I and II are strong
Only argument II is strong
Neither argument I nor II is strong
questions.explanation: The proposal is extreme. Missing essential inputs and the risk of retaliation are concrete reasons against stopping all imports (II strong). Protecting industries does not justify a total ban (I weak). Answer: Only argument II is strong.

questions.question:
Statement: Should all government jobs be given only on the basis of examination marks?

Arguments:
I. Yes, it ensures objective and transparent selection.
II. No, marks alone cannot measure every skill needed for a job.

Which of the following is correct?
options: Only argument I is strong
Both arguments I and II are strong
Only argument II is strong
Neither argument I nor II is strong
questions.explanation: Objectivity is a real benefit (I strong) and marks do not capture every skill (II strong). Answer: Both arguments I and II are strong.

questions.question:
Statement: Should examinations be held online?

Arguments:
I. Yes, since computers are used everywhere nowadays.
II. No, a computer may sometimes hang.

Which of the following is correct?
options: Only argument I is strong
Neither argument I nor II is strong
Only argument II is strong
Both arguments I and II are strong
questions.explanation: "Computers are used everywhere" is vague and does not address exams (I weak); an occasional hang is a minor, fixable issue (II weak). Answer: Neither argument I nor II is strong.

questions.question:
Statement: Should employees be allowed to work from home permanently?

Arguments:
I. Yes, it saves commuting time and costs for both the employees and the company.
II. No, some employees may misuse the freedom.

Which of the following is correct?
options: Only argument I is strong
Only argument II is strong
Both arguments I and II are strong
Neither argument I nor II is strong
questions.explanation: Time and cost savings are specific and important (I strong). "May misuse" is a bare possibility without evidence (II weak). Answer: Only argument I is strong.

questions.question:
Statement: Should the government spend money on space research when many people are poor?

Arguments:
I. Yes, because it makes the country famous.
II. Yes, space technology provides weather forecasts, communication and navigation that also help the poor.

Which of the following is correct?
options: Only argument I is strong
Both arguments I and II are strong
Neither argument I nor II is strong
Only argument II is strong
questions.explanation: Weather forecasts, communication and navigation are concrete benefits (II strong); fame is not a practical benefit (I weak). Answer: Only argument II is strong.

questions.question:
Statement: Should single-use plastic be banned?

Arguments:
I. Yes, it takes hundreds of years to decompose and clogs drains.
II. No, alternatives cost more and small shops may find the switch hard.

Which of the following is correct?
options: Only argument I is strong
Only argument II is strong
Both arguments I and II are strong
Neither argument I nor II is strong
questions.explanation: Long-lasting waste and blocked drains are serious harms (I strong). Higher cost for small shops is a real practical concern (II strong). Answer: Both arguments I and II are strong.
